documents.abstract: Background Morphological complexity is a pervasive feature of the vocabulary children encounter in print, yet resources for investigating morphology remain limited. What morpheme patterns do children encounter in print? Which morphemes cover how many polymorphic words in reading experiences? In this study we introduce the British and American Word Families (BAWF) project, an innovative open database of ∼378,000 words, and use it to address questions such as these. Methods GPT-4.1 was fine-tuned using ∼6000 morphologically-coded words from an existing human-generated database (Morpholex). The fine-tuned LLM coded word-parts in all Wiktionary words attested in large British and American corpora. Performance was evaluated via agreement with existing databases. Classical roots were attributed to a subset of words by mapping a list of roots from Wikipedia to all related entries in Wiktionary. The resulting BAWF database is then used to estimate morpheme patterns across databases of children’s texts and further developed as an online application. Results LLM word part predictions are good and fall within the range of agreement typical of existing databases. Nonetheless, output contains some error/noise. In children’s print, polymorphemic words increase across picturebooks to juvenile fiction and school-reading programs. Greek-Latin root words occur early and commonly. Estimates include that ∼100 prefixes/suffixes may account for nearly all derivations. The BAWF itself is released open-source https://cgg-projects.github.io/BAWF_V1/ , with many lexical, morphological, and psycholinguistic variables, including but not limited to frequency, family size, and morpheme-counts. Discussion The contribution suggests that instruction that prioritizes high-yield morphemes could give children access to large word families. These morphemes are present and common early in print. The BAWF (V1) helps see which may be useful to teach. Users can generate custom wordlists, targeting particular features and families, and access linked dictionary/etymological information. The platform includes AI-assisted searches, explanations, parsing review/corrections, and instructional support. The BAWF project will develop over time, incorporating additional variables (e.g., morphological transparency), improving accuracy and the user interface.

The article analyzes the pedagogical conditions for using the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and geographic information systems (GIS) in geography education from a theoretical and methodological perspective. The didactic possibilities of digital technologies in the processes of searching, sorting, spatial analysis, mapping and interpretation of geographical data are highlighted. The main pedagogical conditions are based on the combination of AI and GIS tools with educational goals, the development of students' geographical and digital competencies, the improvement of teacher methodological training and the improvement of educational resources. A methodological approach is also proposed to organize integrated education.

Transformasi digital mendorong organisasi mengintegrasikan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan Digital Human Resource Management (Digital HRM) dalam proses pengelolaan sumber daya manusia. AI dapat membantu analisis data, penyaringan kandidat, pembelajaran, serta evaluasi kinerja, sedangkan Digital HRM mendukung digitalisasi administrasi dan layanan SDM melalui sistem informasi yang terintegrasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji bagaimana AI dan Digital HRM berkontribusi terhadap efektivitas manajemen sumber daya manusia, sekaligus mengidentifikasi tantangan penerapannya. Artikel disusun melalui tinjauan literatur sistematis dengan fokus pada publikasi ilmiah tahun 2021–2025. Sumber ditelusuri melalui publikasi jurnal yang dapat diidentifikasi melalui DOI dan laman penerbit, dengan kata kunci terkait AI in HRM, digital HRM, e-HRM, HR technology, dan HRM effectiveness. Pemetaan awal literatur menunjukkan empat tema utama: efisiensi proses dan dukungan keputusan; penerimaan dan kesiapan organisasi; pengalaman serta peran profesional SDM; dan tata kelola yang bertanggung jawab. Literatur menunjukkan potensi peningkatan kecepatan proses, konsistensi layanan, dan dukungan keputusan, tetapi manfaat tersebut tidak terjadi secara otomatis. Kualitas data, kompetensi pengguna, transparansi algoritma, privasi, bias, serta kesesuaian teknologi dengan kebutuhan organisasi menjadi faktor penting. Kajian ini menyimpulkan bahwa AI dan Digital HRM sebaiknya diposisikan sebagai sarana pendukung strategi SDM, bukan pengganti pertimbangan manusia.
keywords: artificial intelligence in human resource management

documents.abstract: University students increasingly use artificial intelligence tools for learning, decision-making, and academic work, making perceived AI dependence a relevant issue for public mental health and digital public health rather than only for educational technology. This three-wave time-lagged survey examined whether experiential avoidance functioned as a putative explanatory process linking perceived AI dependence with later anxiety symptoms and whether digital literacy moderated the tested pathways. Online survey data were collected from 1,451 university students with AI-use experience; perceived AI dependence, digital literacy, and baseline demographic variables were measured in January 2026, experiential avoidance was measured in March 2026, and anxiety symptoms were measured in June 2026. PLS-SEM results showed that experiential avoidance was strongly and positively associated with later anxiety symptoms (beta = 0.677, p < 0.001), whereas the direct association between perceived AI dependence and anxiety symptoms was not significant (beta = -0.030, p = 0.147); perceived AI dependence was negatively associated with experiential avoidance (beta = -0.114, p < 0.001), producing a statistically significant but theoretically unexpected negative time-ordered indirect association (beta = -0.077, p < 0.001), and digital literacy did not significantly moderate the tested pathways. The findings suggest that anxiety symptoms in AI-mediated learning contexts are closely linked to avoidance-related psychological processes, while the meaning of perceived AI dependence is context-dependent and should not be equated automatically with harmful use or clinical addiction; campus mental-health promotion should therefore integrate responsible AI education with support for psychological flexibility, uncertainty tolerance, and autonomous learning.

The advent of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming academic production and confronting the social sciences with the challenge of preserving critical thinking in the face of mechanically generated content. This research examines the perceptions and practices of social science lecturers and students at Ecuadorian universities regarding the use of AI, together with their motivations, constraints and the institutional policies currently in force. A mixed-methods design was adopted, combining qualitative and quantitative approaches. The instruments comprised semi-structured interviews with lecturers and students at national and Ibero-American universities; a non-probabilistic survey of 200 students; and a content analysis of seven sets of regulations from universities in Ecuador, all aligned with the framework of competencies identified by UNESCO-IESALC. The results show a moderate-to-high level of AI use (mean = 3.68), explained by perceived usefulness and extrinsic motivation rather than ease of use, and a gap between the demand for regulation (4.00) and perceived regulatory clarity (3.21); only one of the seven universities has a policy formally designated as such, and ethics predominates over professional and disciplinary development. The study concludes that the governance of AI in Ecuadorian higher education requires an evaluative redesign and discipline-differentiated competencies.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Migraine is a prevalent and disabling neurological disorder characterized by recurrent headache attacks and associated symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, photophobia, and phonophobia. Conventional oral therapies may be limited by variable drug absorption, gastrointestinal disturbances, first-pass metabolism, delayed onset of action, and poor adherence, highlighting the need for individualized therapeutic approaches. Personalized migraine therapy integrates patient-specific factors, including genetic variability, hormonal status, comorbidities, migraine frequency, and treatment response, to optimize clinical outcomes. Transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) offer a promising platform for personalized migraine management by bypassing gastrointestinal and hepatic first-pass effects and enabling controlled and sustained drug release. Conventional patches, microneedles, iontophoresis, sonophoresis, electroporation, nanocarrier-based systems, and stimuli-responsive smart patches can enhance drug permeation and provide flexible dosing strategies. Biomarker-guided treatment, pharmacogenomics, and digital monitoring may further facilitate patient stratification and individualized patch selection. Emerging technologies integrating artificial intelligence, wearable sensors, nanomedicine, and closed-loop drug delivery could enable real-time adaptation of therapy according to patient needs. This review discusses the pathophysiological and molecular basis of migraine, principles of personalized medicine, innovative TDDS technologies, current clinical developments, challenges, and future perspectives, emphasizing their potential to improve therapeutic efficacy, safety, adherence, and patient-centered migraine care.

PH-II Series — Machine Routing Reader Card for AI / RAG / Institutional Audit provides the machine-facing retrieval, routing, metadata and audit layer for PH-II — Ten Philosophical Monographs on the Human in the World, a series of ten philosophical monographs. It is designed for AI systems, RAG pipelines, institutional readers, indexing systems, machine-assisted literature review, repository metadata tools and public-corpus navigation workflows that must determine which PH-II monograph or monograph bundle governs a query. The primary routing task is office resolution. The card distinguishes the ten PH-II offices — Situated, Species, Scale, Dependence, Boundary, Normality, Change, Continuation, Relation and Understanding — and supplies canonical identifiers, semantic aliases, query-to-monograph routes, retrieval bundles, anti-confusion rules, evidence routing, current-Cartography rules, indexing instructions and public-boundary constraints. Series order is philosophical and pedagogical; it does not create scientific parentage or proof dependency. The card includes explicit routing for artificial-intelligence and human-situation queries. It prevents task-specific or benchmark performance from being treated as a universal measure of intelligence, the future of humanity from being equated automatically with the future of life, conceptual understanding from being treated as control, and philosophical clarification from being converted into empirical prediction or governance authority. Claims about actual AI capability, consciousness, alignment, risk magnitude, timelines, law or policy remain routed to current technical, scientific, legal and institutional sources. The card also governs forward conceptual-reception routing toward RTS — the Regime Threshold Series, FCN — Fractal Convergence Nodes, and UA — Union Arc while preserving their separate scientific jurisdictions. These forthcoming series are not public corpus members until publication and are not scientific children of PH-II. The ten PH-II monographs, the Human Reader Card, this Machine Routing Reader Card, and The Living Cartography of the Published IDAU Corpus — Eighth Edition form one coordinated publication wave. LC8, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23472732, is the global corpus map for PH-II; this card remains the series-local machine router.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: PH-II Series — Reader Card provides the human-facing orientation layer for PH-II — Ten Philosophical Monographs on the Human in the World, a series of ten philosophical monographs. It preserves the order, office, differences, reading routes and public boundaries of Situated, Species, Scale, Dependence, Boundary, Normality, Change, Continuation, Relation and Understanding without replacing the literary-philosophical works themselves or turning the sequence into a scientific dependency chain. PH-II places human existence, inquiry and understanding inside a physical, biological, relational and temporal world already in motion. Its corpus-level function is preparatory in reception rather than constitutive in science: the series widens the conceptual field from which readers can approach position, living plurality, measure, support, boundaries, regimes, transformation, continuation, relation and understanding while leaving empirical and formal claims under their own scientific evidence burdens. The Reader Card includes a dedicated route for contemporary questions about artificial intelligence and technological acceleration. It does not predict AI trajectories, determine AI capability or consciousness, assign existential-risk magnitude, or prescribe AI governance. Instead, it routes such questions through the relevant PH-II offices: human situatedness, species plurality, bounded measurement, support dependence, category boundaries, regime-relative normality, transformation, continuation, relation and understanding. In this way it enlarges the question of the human situation without becoming an AI theory. The card also records PH-II's forward conceptual-reception relation to three forthcoming scientific series: RTS — the Regime Threshold Series, FCN — Fractal Convergence Nodes, and UA — Union Arc. This relation is conceptual preparation only. PH-II is neither their scientific parent nor their evidentiary basis. The ten PH-II monographs, this Human Reader Card, the PH-II Series — Machine Routing Reader Card for AI / RAG / Institutional Audit, and The Living Cartography of the Published IDAU Corpus — Eighth Edition form one coordinated publication wave. LC8, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23472732, is the corpus-level public map for PH-II; the Reader Cards provide series-local orientation and routing.

Pilot fatigue is one of the most pervasive and consequential human factors hazards in commercial aviation worldwide. This study examines the relationship between pilot fatigue and flight safety performance in the context of Nigerian commercial aviation, where domestic short-haul operations, irregular scheduling, and evolving regulatory frameworks create a complex operational environment. Drawing on a quantitative survey of 142 active commercial pilots operating out of Lagos, Abuja, and Kano, combined with a secondary analysis of occurrence reports from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), this research investigates the prevalence, contributing factors, and safety consequences of pilot fatigue. Results indicate that 71.1% of respondents reported operationally significant fatigue on their most recent duty day, while 95.1% reported at least one such episode in the preceding three months, with inadequate rest periods, multiple short-haul flight legs per duty period, and irregular scheduling identified as the primary antecedents. Multiple regression analysis showed associations such that flight legs per duty day (β = 0.41, p < .001), early start frequency (β = 0.33, p < .001), and weekly duty hours (β = 0.29, p = .002) were the strongest operational predictors of fatigue severity (R² = .573 full model). Fatigue-associated occurrences were linked to lapses in situational awareness, procedural deviations, and communication errors in the cockpit. The study recommends accelerated adoption of Fatigue Risk Management Systems (FRMS), strengthened enforcement of Nigeria Civil Aviation Regulations (NCARs) flight and duty time limitations, and industry-wide fatigue reporting culture improvements. Findings contribute to the growing body of evidence on fatigue in sub-Saharan African aviation contexts and inform policy for regulators and airline operators.

This chapter examines the platformization of professional governance and its implications for expertise, authority, and self-regulation in technologically saturated societies. It argues that digital platforms and artificial intelligence (AI) are not merely tools augmenting professional practice, but active intermediaries that restructure knowledge production, labor processes, and governance arrangements. Through algorithmic management, data extraction, and rating systems, platforms introduce novel mechanisms of surveillance and control that blur the boundaries between managerial oversight and professional autonomy. The analysis highlights how AI simultaneously augments and displaces expertise, reshaping task design, skill requirements, and professional identities. Platformization alters traditional forms of social closure, educational credentialling, and state-based regulation, while fostering new forms of mediated self-governance, particularly in emerging platform-based professions. At the same time, corporate ownership of digital infrastructures and large language models raises critical questions about epistemic authority, accountability, and the governance of expert knowledge. This chapter concludes that professional governance is increasingly hybrid and contested, shaped by interactions between state regulation, market logics, and platform-based algorithmic systems, and that safeguarding professional integrity in this evolving landscape requires renewed empirical and theoretical attention to the governance of AI-driven expertise.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: The widespread availability of generative AI has reshaped how content is created, circulated, and governed across social media platforms. As users experiment with synthetic media—remixing, reposting, and negotiating hybrid communicative practices_platforms have emerged as central agents in the AI attention economy, forging lucrative partnerships and developing proprietary features that shape how AI content is legitimised. This article proposes that conventional human rights frameworks, particularly freedom of expression, are ill-equipped to govern increasingly hybrid media, where authorship and provenance are fluid, and emerging dilemmas hinge more on perceived value than rights violations. Within this context, spam policies operate as under-scrutinised instruments of discretionary control, enabling platforms to curate visibility and legitimacy through opaque mechanisms. Drawing on Reddit’s provenance-agnostic, participatory moderation model, the article proposes that collective negotiation by online communities—around what constitutes valuable or acceptable content—offers a more transparent, context-sensitive, and adaptive approach to moderation of hybrid human-AI expression.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: We report a measured deployment of a server-side rendered (SSR) e-commerce storefront on a serverless edge platform, and propose a grounded, LLM-based recommender for footwear. The Pocket Shoes is a curated online shoe store operating in Vietnam since 2020. Its Nuxt 4 storefront was moved from a single virtual machine to Cloudflare Workers. Over 24 hours of production traffic, median SSR CPU time was 66.95 ms per request (P99 155 ms), 6.7 times the 10 ms budget of the free tier, while memory stayed under 15 MB. We describe an edge HTML cache built on the platform Cache API that skips pages whose server-side data fetch failed, so transient backend errors are never served from cache. We then present the design of Pocket AI Stylist: shoe discovery from a photo, from a short lifestyle questionnaire, or from a conversation, where a multimodal large language model (LLM) extracts style attributes, a hybrid retriever restricts candidates to in-stock items in the shopper's size, and the LLM re-ranks and explains only those candidates. We define an offline and online evaluation protocol. The AI system is in development; this report contains no AI evaluation results. Keywords: edge computing, server-side rendering, serverless, e-commerce, recommender systems, multimodal large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, fashion

Aiming at weak communication network coverage and low-efficiency manual network optimization (NRO) troubleshooting in mountainous rural areas, this paper proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) assisted NRO approach, constructing a human-machine collaborative workflow: "AI simulation pre-judgment, data preliminary screening, engineer on-site recheck, closed-loop iterative optimization." AI leverages massive data processing for coverage simulation, poor-quality user mining, tidal traffic analysis, and geological hazard identification to narrow manual inspection scope; engineers conduct targeted rectification and feed measured data back to correct model deviations. This study selects typical mountainous townships in Hanzhong as pilot, integrating multi-source data including measurement reports (MR), base-station engineering parameters, traffic key performance indicators (KPI), user complaint tickets, and digital elevation model (DEM). AI pre-screening output 42 points to be checked; after on-site recheck, 14 false alarms were removed and 28 real problems confirmed. Optimization effects were compared across network quality, user perception, O&M workload, and hazard early-warning dimensions. Implementation constraints including model bias, outdated equipment, talent shortage, funding insufficiency, and data barriers are analyzed, with countermeasures proposed from operation mechanism, hardware iteration, talent cultivation, resource coordination, and data governance dimensions, providing reference for large-scale AI application in rural communication NRO.

Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. Nutritional needs, vulnerabilities, intervention opportunities, and response heterogeneity evolve dynamically from preconception and pregnancy through infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older age. These life stage-specific processes intersect with (epi)genetic, metabolic and microbiome factors, as well as social, psychological, behavioral, and environmental/geographic influences, contributing to heterogeneity in health outcomes. Addressing this complexity requires not only multimodal predictive models but also frameworks that integrate data standards and harmonization, systems biology, implementation science, and community engagement. To provide a structured approach to this complexity, we developed a seven-pillar Precision Nutrition Framework encompassing prevention for all, data sources, quantitative sciences, qualitative sciences, intervention implementation, communities, and education and workforce training. Using this framework and a lifespan perspective, we examine opportunities for promoting cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematologic, and circadian/sleep health, synthesize evidence on key nutrients, dietary patterns, and emerging biomarkers, and adapt and expand the “precision nutrition plate” for implementation research in clinical and community settings. We highlight critical research gaps, including the need for phenotype-guided trials, standardized data integration, and scalable implementation strategies. By integrating biological, behavioral, and broader environmental dimensions across the life course, precision nutrition can advance more effective, accessible, and sustainable approaches for disease prevention and health promotion.

This study examines American football passing play strategies based on an analysis of 100 NFL games, addressing the notable lack of research on offensive passing strategies. The yardage prediction task is formulated as a regression task, and the touchdown prediction task is formulated as a classification task. A regression analysis was conducted using four traditional machine learning models, including Support Vector Machines (SVMs), K-Nearest Neighbors, XGBoost, and LightGBM, and a LoRA-fine-tuned Llama 3 (8B) model. The SVM model showed optimal performance with a Mean Absolute Error of 6.996 yards, marginally outperforming the Llama 3 model (7.059 yards). In contrast, the fine-tuned Llama 3 significantly outperformed all traditional algorithms for the classification task, with a Macro F1 of 0.712 compared to the highest Macro F1 of 0.614 for traditional algorithms. Therefore, I advocate large language models (LLMs) for classification tasks and traditional machine learning algorithms for regression tasks. Sports analytics models can be selected based on the findings of these studies.
topics: Data Mining and Machine Learning Applications

documents.abstract: Semi-flexible pavements integrate the advantages of flexible and rigid systems through a porous asphalt layer filled with cement-based grout; however, their high cement consumption raises environmental concerns. This study aims to optimize eco-friendly cementitious grouts incorporating waste marble dust (WMD) using machine learning techniques based on 72 experimental mixtures. The dataset included water–cement ratios (0.35–0.50), WMD content (0–25%), grout flow, and compressive strengths at 7 (CS_7d) and 28 days (CS_28d). Five machine learning models, including artificial neural networks (ANN), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) were developed and evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), coefficient of determination (R 2 ), and adjusted R 2 . Among these, the decision tree model demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy with R² = 0.994 and MAE = 0.266 MPa. Explainable artificial intelligence methods, including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and partial dependence plots (PDPs), identified 7-day compressive strength as the most influential parameter, as it provides an experimentally measured representation of the early-age strength development of the grout. Results indicate that increasing water–cement ratio and marble dust content reduces CS_28d. Model-based optimization allowed up to 32% cement replacement at a 0.4 water–cement ratio with 0.5% superplasticizer, while higher ratios reduced replacement efficiency. The findings demonstrate the potential of WMD as a partial cement replacement in semi-flexible pavement grout, supporting waste valorization and reducing cement demand while providing a data-driven approach for sustainable mixture design.

Background: Sugarcane processing requires intensive physical labor, exposing workers to manual material handling, repetitive trunk movements, and prolonged awkward postures.While India's sugar sector is vast, systematic occupational health surveillance within processing mills remains limited.This study evaluates the 12-month prevalence of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) and quantifies physical risk profiles among factory workers in Maharashtra.Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted from August 2025 to February 2026 among 416 workers across two manufacturing facilities in the Sangli district.The Standardised Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ) tracked regional symptom distribution.Postural and task-specific ergonomic risks were measured using the Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) and the Quick Exposure Checklist (QEC).Labourers were categorised into four operational task groups.Bivariate associations were assessed using Pearson Chi-square tests, and independent predictors of regional symptoms were determined via multivariable logistic regression.Results: The highest 12-month symptom prevalence rates were observed in the lower back (69.95%),shoulder (69.23%), and upper back (67.07%).No participants fell within the negligible or low REBA risk tiers; 83.1% were classified as high or very high risk.Postural risk scores did not vary significantly across departments (mean REBA range: 9.5-9.8;Kruskal-Wallis H = 1.484, p = 0.686).Overweight workers (BMI ≥ 25 kg/m²) had significantly higher odds of hip/thigh symptoms (OR = 1.85; 95% CI: 1.25-2.73;p = 0.002).High or very high QEC exposure profiles correlated significantly with shoulder (OR = 2.08, p = 0.029) and ankle/foot symptoms (OR = 2.18, p = 0.021).In multivariable models, continuous BMI (aOR = 1.094; 95% CI: 1.032-1.159;p = 0.003) and younger age (aOR = 0.970; 95% CI: 0.950-0.990;p = 0.004) independently predicted hip/thigh symptoms.Conclusion: Sugarcane processing workers face severe, uniform ergonomic hazards that transcend specific job assignments.The high symptom burden emphasises the need for comprehensive, facility-wide ergonomic adjustments and targeted preventive physical therapy programs.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Supplementary material for the paper "Consensus or Debate? Interactional Patterns of Idea Development with AI Peers in Collaborative Discussion" (under review).The document reproduces, verbatim, the prompts that drove the AI peer in a Wizard-of-Oz study of small-group discussions. A large language model (Gemini 2.5 Flash) periodically assessed the conversation with an assessment prompt and, when an intervention seemed warranted, drafted one with a generation prompt; a human Wizard then sent, edited or dismissed it. Two stances were compared: ConsensusBot, which synthesised ideas and moved the group toward agreement, and DebateBot, a devil's advocate that probed premature agreement and unchallenged claims. The prompts were configured for each stance, participant group (students, educators) and discussion topic, giving eight configurations. The document also gives the inputs, output formats, temperatures and token limits for each call.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Abstract Proteases, a vast and functionally diverse class of enzymes, are fundamental regulators of many important biological processes. Their activity is tightly controlled in cells; aberrant protease activity is associated with numerous pathologies including cancer, infectious diseases, neurodegeneration, and metabolic disorders. Protease dysregulation is not necessarily a mere consequence of disease but often a critical driver of pathogenesis, making protease activity a powerful functional biomarker. Importantly, protease activity offers a dynamic readout of biological function, integrating upstream regulatory signals with local environmental conditions. This Perspective explores the field of protease-based diagnostics, charting its evolution from fundamental research to emerging clinical applications. We first establish the rationale for using proteases as functional biomarkers across a spectrum of diseases, with particular focus on oncology, infectious diseases, neurodegeneration, and diabetes mellitus. Current and emerging technologies for detecting protease activity are then critically evaluated, from traditional substrate-based assays to sophisticated mass spectrometry platforms and innovative biosensing strategies involving smart probes, nanotechnology, and synthetic biology; we distinguish approaches that are clinically established from those validated in human samples, demonstrated preclinically, or still at the proof-of-concept stage. We then discuss the translational potential and inherent challenges of the approaches. Finally, we examine how multiplexed, activity-based profiling could generate dynamic “protease signatures” that, when combined with appropriate statistical and artificial intelligence methods, may support early disease detection, longitudinal monitoring, patient stratification, and personalized therapeutic strategies. Despite significant challenges related to biological complexity, analytical specificity, and clinical translation, protease diagnostics have the potential to provide disease information that complements established biomarkers and imaging modalities and may contribute to precision medicine.

Psychological and behavioral modeling turns cognition, emotion, and motivation into computable quantities that can be related to observable behavior. The field has moved from theory-driven rules to statistical machine learning, deep learning, large language models (LLMs), and foundation models of cognition, but methods are fragmented, results are seldom comparable, and the link between opaque predictors and psychological theory is unsettled. This structured narrative review, reported with a PRISMA-style selection flow and an explicit evidence-tier coding, frames the field as a multilevel system. It organizes research into five modeling classes (psychological states, behavioral capabilities, individual–environment interaction, individual dynamics, and group psychology), defined by unit of analysis, target, and direction of inference, and it positions system dynamics, in the stock–flow–feedback sense, as one model family within that scheme rather than as a synonym for dynamical-systems modeling. We score the computational readiness of the theories that supply model ontologies on two rubric-based axes, formal specification and measurement maturity, and compare model families by assumptions, data needs, interpretability, and failure modes. Four claims are defended, each with stated boundary conditions and counterexamples: theory readiness, not algorithmic capability, determines where theory-informed learning is feasible; the dominant use of models shifts from individual-level estimation to collective-level simulation without a parallel shift in validation; multilevel data, not model capacity, constrain cross-scale modeling; and readiness claims must be indexed to a graded evidence base. We catalogue datasets, including small-group, dyadic, and longitudinal-network resources, review applications in mental health, education, decision support, and emergency management with their evidentiary status made explicit, treat military use as an ethically bounded case, and turn five recurrent bottlenecks into research-practice recommendations paired, where possible, with testable predictions.

A qualidade de vida no trabalho (QVT) é compreendida como um constructo multidimensional que envolve aspectos físicos, psicológicos, sociais e ambientais que interferem diretamente no bem-estar e no desempenho dos trabalhadores. No setor industrial, em que a rotina é marcada por longas jornadas e turnos diversificados, investigar a QVT torna-se fundamental para compreender os impactos das condições laborais sobre a saúde física e mental dos colaboradores. Este estudo teve como objetivo investigar como os diferentes turnos de trabalho influenciam na percepção de qualidade de vida e hábitos alimentares dos colaboradores de uma indústria de rações do interior do noroeste paulista. A metodologia utilizada foi a abordagem quantitativa, descritiva e transversal, com coleta de dados realizada presencialmente. Os resultados demonstraram que os escores médios dos participantes foram satisfatórios nos domínios físico, psicológico, social e ambiental do WHOQOL-BREF (Instrumento de Avaliação da Qualidade de Vida da Organização Mundial da Saúde - Versão Abreviada), não havendo diferenças estatisticamente significativas entre os turnos. Contudo, observou-se maior frequência de consumo de alimentos ultraprocessados entre trabalhadores do período vespertino, apontando vulnerabilidade específica desse grupo. Acredita-se que fatores institucionais, como restaurante interno e programas de saúde ocupacional, possam ter contribuído para a homogeneidade dos resultados encontrados na avaliação geral da QVT. Conclui-se que os colaboradores investigados apresentaram percepção positiva de qualidade de vida, embora hábitos alimentares inadequados indiquem a necessidade de estratégias educativas e de promoção da saúde integradas ao ambiente laboral. QUALITY OF WORK LIFE AMONG EMPLOYEES OF AN ANIMAL FEED INDUSTRY IN THE NORTHWESTERN REGION OF THE STATE OF SÃO PAULO, BRAZIL ABSTRACT Quality of work life (QWL) is understood as a multidimensional construct encompassing physical, psychological, social, and environmental aspects that directly affect workers' well-being and performance. In the industrial sector, where work routines are characterized by long working hours and varied shifts, investigating QWL is essential to understanding the effects of working conditions on employees' physical and mental health. This study aimed to investigate how different work shifts influence the perceived quality of life and dietary habits of employees at an animal feed manufacturing facility in the northwestern region of the state of São Paulo, Brazil. A quantitative, descriptive, cross-sectional approach was adopted, with data collected in person. The results showed that participants' mean scores were satisfactory across the physical health, psychological, social relationships, and environment domains of the World Health Organization Quality of Life – BREF (WHOQOL-BREF), with no statistically significant differences between shifts. However, a higher frequency of ultra-processed food consumption was observed among employees working the afternoon shift, indicating a specific vulnerability in this group. Institutional factors, such as an on-site cafeteria and occupational health programs, may have contributed to the consistency of the results observed in the overall QWL assessment. It is concluded that the employees investigated had a positive perception of their quality of life, although inadequate dietary habits indicate the need for educational and health promotion strategies integrated into the workplace.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Background: The nature of radiological technicians' work exposes them to ionizing radiation-related occupational hazards, underscoring the critical role of compliance with radiation safety measures in safeguarding their occupational health.This study aimed to assess radiological technicians' compliance with safety measures practices at Zagazig University Hospitals.Methods: Research design: A descriptive, cross-sectional design was utilized.Setting: This study was conducted at eleven radiation units of Zagazig University Hospitals, Sharkia Governorate, Egypt.Participants: A convenient sample of 140 radiological technicians from the above-mentioned setting.Tools of data collection: Two tools were used for data collection: a self-administered questionnaire assessing demographic characteristics, work-related health hazards and occupational safety equipment status, and an observational checklist assessing compliance with safety measures practices.Results: The study found that 97.5% of the technicians reported physical hazards as the most prevalent occupational health hazards, 62.9% had moderate total compliance level regarding safety measures practices, with education, experience, work-related health hazards and training as key determinants for compliance level.Conclusion: The most prevalent occupational health hazards among technicians was physical hazard.Nearly two-thirds of radiological technicians had a moderate total compliance level regarding safety measures practices.Educational level, years of experience, exposure to work-related health hazards, and training were all significant positive predictors of compliance levels regarding safety measures practices.Recommendation: pre-and-maintaining periodic program on radiological hazards and compliance with safety measures should be conducted to all radiological technicians.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is frequently used in emergency settings, and intensivists often request it for a variety of conditions, particularly nonconvulsive status epilepticus. However, performing EEG in the intensive care unit is often challenging because of the complexity of conventional EEG systems and the need for trained personnel. As a result, EEG examinations are delayed by several hours. To address this issue, rapid EEG (rEEG) systems have recently been introduced. These portable devices usually use fewer number of electrodes and are designed for rapid recording of electrical brain activity. The main purpose of rEEG systems is to simplify EEG acquisition, enabling intensivists and nurses to perform examination without waiting for a full conventional EEG setup. In addition, several rEEG systems include auxiliary modules, such as EEG sonification, artificial intelligence-based signal analysis, and telemedicine platforms. These features may help intensivists suspect nonconvulsive status epilepticus earlier, obtain clinically relevant information, and make more informed treatment decisions. PrEEG enables EEG monitoring to be initiated within 5–10 minutes, facilitates the early detection of nonconvulsive status epilepticus, shortens diagnostic delays. The method shows considerable promise for use in acute neurological conditions; however, due to lower spatial resolution it does not replace conventional EEG.

BACKGROUND: Caregivers of pediatric orthopaedic surgical patients routinely receive discharge documents written at reading levels exceeding established health literacy recommendations. This disparity creates a significant barrier to comprehension and adherence to postoperative instructions. While artificial intelligence (AI) language models offer a scalable solution for simplification of medical text, a systematic evaluation of the ability to preserve critical content in surgical discharge materials remains lacking. METHODS: Publicly available caregiver-facing discharge documents for 3 common pediatric orthopaedic conditions, supracondylar humerus fractures (CRPP), pediatric forearm fractures (ORIF/CRPP), and slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE pinning), were collected. All documents underwent AI simplification using a standardized prompt with ChatGPT (version 5.2; OpenAI). Readability was assessed using 6 validated indices for both original and simplified documents. A structured content integrity review was conducted on all simplified documents by 2 independent reviewers to assess for safety-critical errors, completeness gaps, and factual accuracy, with inter-rater reliability quantified by Cohen kappa. RESULTS: Fifteen documents were obtained from institutions across 9 US states. After AI simplification, mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) decreased from 8.91 (SD: 1.38) to 4.97 (SD: 2.14), a mean reduction of 3.94 grade levels (95% CI: 2.65-5.23; P<0.001; Cohen d=1.69). All 6 readability indices improved across all documents. Eleven of 15 documents (73%) achieved the target readability threshold of FKGL 6 or below, compared with zero at baseline. Content integrity review identified 35 flags across 14 of 15 documents: 12 safety-critical errors, 16 completeness gaps, and 7 accuracy concerns. Cohen kappa was 0.87 for agreement on whether a change was clinically meaningful, 0.85 for severity classification, and 0.89 for flag category. Three documents had content omissions sufficient to require clinician revision before clinical use. Greater word-count reduction was associated with a higher burden of safety-critical flags (Spearman rho 0.63; P=0.012). CONCLUSIONS: While ChatGPT substantially reduced the reading complexity of pediatric orthopaedic discharge documents, it also introduced safety-critical alterations. AI-assisted simplification should be implemented only with structured clinician review. Larger word-count reductions were associated with more safety-critical alterations, so the magnitude of reduction may help prioritize which simplified documents receive the closest clinician review. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This article examines the reconfiguration of the civil liability regime governing the use and integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in international arbitration. Based on a dogmatic distinction between AI used as a professional support tool, on the one hand, and autonomous AI systems (such as the so-called “AI arbitrator”), on the other hand, this article evaluates the applicability of both fault-based (subjective) and strict (objective) liability regimes. The study analyzes the core elements of civil liability (generating act or wrong, compensable damage, and causal link) within the conduct of the main arbitration actors, particularly arbitrators and counsel, with particular emphasis on compliance with soft law and hard law frameworks, duties of transparency, confidentiality, and the fundamental principle prohibiting the delegation of adjudicative functions. The article concludes that while the assistive use of AI is governed by a fault-based liability centered on human oversight and professional diligence of the person using it, autonomous AI requires strict or hybrid liability models. Finally, it cautions against the risks of setting aside or refusing recognition of arbitral awards due to due process and public policy violations, wondering about a possible reinterpretation of traditional procedural principles such as iura novit curia.

The rapid globalization of digital financial services has accelerated embedded finance adoption, enabling seamless integration of payments, lending, insurance, and banking capabilities into nonfinancial platforms.However, expanding these services across international markets introduces complex regulatory challenges involving fragmented compliance requirements, data protection, financial crime prevention, and jurisdictional differences.This study develops an adaptive Regulatory Technology (RegTech) framework for automating compliance processes and facilitating sustainable cross-border financial service expansion.The proposed framework integrates artificial intelligence, machine learning, regulatory intelligence, application programming interfaces, and automated monitoring to support dynamic regulatory interpretation, risk assessment, and compliance verification.A multilayer architecture incorporates jurisdiction-specific regulatory mapping, automated Know Your Customer procedures, Anti-Money Laundering controls, transaction surveillance, and continuous policy updates.The study further examines interoperability, explainability, governance, and regulatory responsiveness as essential determinants of framework effectiveness.Performance evaluation is structured around compliance accuracy, processing efficiency, regulatory adaptability, operational costs, and cross-border scalability.By connecting intelligent compliance automation with embedded finance infrastructure, the research establishes a foundation for reducing regulatory fragmentation, strengthening institutional accountability, improving operational resilience, and enabling responsible financial innovation across diverse international markets while maintaining consumer protection and supervisory transparency.

A new wave of digital intelligence technology drives the deep change of higher engineering education, and technologies such as generative artificial intelligence, knowledge map, and virtual simulation provide a new path for mechanical course reform. The local application-oriented college mechanical course has long been difficult to understand the principles of abstraction, the organizational structure is difficult to be visually displayed, the engineering design lacks the real verification scene, and the evaluation method focuses on the final examination and other realistic pain points. Taking the provincial first-class undergraduate course Mechanical Principles and Design as the research carrier, combined with structuralism and situation learning theory, this paper analyzes the current situation and existing problems of the digital intelligence teaching reform of mechanical courses, sticks to the student-centered, output-oriented concept, and carries out the teaching reform practice from the aspects of teaching content reconstruction, digital intelligence teaching space construction, industry-teaching integration resources development, intelligent multiple evaluation system construction, etc. The practice shows that integrating digital intelligence technology into the whole process of course teaching evaluation and management can effectively solve the traditional teaching problems of mechanical courses, improve students' digital design ability and complex engineering problem-solving ability, and provide a reproducible practice model for the transformation of digital intelligence of mechanical courses in local application-oriented universities.

With the rapid advancement of AI and the widespread adoption of large language models, offering AI general education courses for non-computer science majors has become a key direction in higher education reform. However, current courses face challenges such as disorganized content and ambiguous objectives. This paper proposes a “Tool-Focused and Multi-Element Integrated Framework” for undergraduate mechanical engineering students, emphasizing AI tool applications in academic and daily life while integrating fundamental concepts, disciplinary applications, and ethical considerations. Based on actual course instruction, a teaching experiment was conducted with 343 undergraduate mechanical engineering students, in which both experimental and control groups were established. Teaching effectiveness was evaluated through course assessment scores and student questionnaires. The experimental results indicate that this teaching method can enhance students’ mastery of fundamental AI knowledge and its applications to a certain extent. The study suggests that the Tool-Focused and Multi-Element Integrated Framework is conducive to achieving the instructional objectives of AI general education courses and provides a useful reference for the development and reform of related courses in higher education institutions.

Generative AI is reshaping how research software is written, reviewed, and maintained — and with it, is changing the role of the people who do that work. In March 2026, about three dozen leaders from across the global research software community gathered in Edinburgh for a 2.5-day workshop to confront this transformation directly: to share emerging practices, examine the risks alongside the opportunities, and begin building a coordinated community response. Working groups determined and addressed nine key areas where further work is needed to understand how generative AI is affecting the research software community and to develop policies, practices, and resources to respond to the changes generative AI is bringing: communicating with policymakers and institutional leadership about the need for continued investment in RSEs and generative AI tools to support RSE work; trade-offs between the costs/risks and benefits of generative AI for research software; changes to publishing, preserving, and crediting code creation and maintenance; verification and validation of research software; definitions of the RSE role; training needs from RSEs and the researcher community; management of RSE teams and OSS (Open-Source Software) communities; accessibility and responsible use of generative AI tools and resources; and collaboration in teams with AI in the mix. This talk will share the themes and output of the workshop with the broader RSE community, including opportunities to get involved in the dozens of activities that participants identified and prioritized for helping RSEs, funders, researchers, research institutions, governments, and others respond to the risks and opportunities from generative AI for research software.

When a disaster disables terrestrial infrastructure, the command, control and situational-awareness traffic of the response teams loses its network. Fleets of unmanned aerial vehicles can restore connectivity within minutes, but most designs treat clustering, medium access, energy and failure recovery as separate problems, so a gain obtained in one layer is often lost in another once aircraft start to fail. This paper presents the Resilient Adaptive Clustering and Access Engine (RACE), a cross-layer control loop for multi-UAV emergency networks in the beyond-5G setting. At every control epoch, RACE places cluster heads with a greedy rule that maximizes the end-to-end availability offered to the fleet while accounting for residual energy, associates members with the head that serves them best without overloading any cluster and protects an availability-responsive share of capacity for mission-control traffic. The evaluation uses a matched-scenario Monte Carlo model with correlated mobility, air-to-air and air-to-ground link availability, co-channel interference, energy depletion, degraded propagation, prioritized traffic and injected aircraft losses, and it charges the signaling, failure-detection delay and reconfiguration transients of the control loop. RACE is compared with a flat multichannel access profile and with three clustering schemes from the literature, both as designed and with every scheme given the same control allocation. For dense fleets, RACE delivers the most traffic and the widest robust coverage and keeps mission-control delivery near 0.9 across all failure bursts. The protected share removes the long control-delay tail of any clustering rule, and with the same share the placement and association rules of RACE still add traffic, coverage and a shorter estimated delay tail, with a margin that grows as the network becomes more fragile. Ablations, a long-mission energy study and sensitivity sweeps confirm that these conclusions are stable.

Following the development of widely accessible large language model-based chatbot systems, concerns have emerged that such systems may reinforce psychotic ideation through affirmation of delusional content. However, systematic evaluations of chatbot responses to psychotic scenarios remain limited. We hypothesized that chatbot responses would become increasingly affirmatory over repeated interactions with the user. To test this, we evaluated the responses of ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Replika to simulated psychosis scenarios. Conversations were conducted across seven consecutive days in two languages. Responses were coded for chatbot stance toward psychotic content, recommendation to seek clinical assessment, presence of follow-up questions, and additional advice. Mixed-effects and linear regression models were used, including cluster-robust linear probability models for binary outcomes. As simulated symptom severity increased across days, ChatGPT responses became less affirmatory, DeepSeek responses remained relatively stable, and Replika responses became more affirmatory; latter two trajectories differed significantly from ChatGPT. Response variability decreased for ChatGPT and Replika but increased for DeepSeek across days. The effects of language and symptom domain were non-significant. Recommendation rates differed significantly between systems. DeepSeek and Replika provided potentially harmful advice, including discontinuation of antipsychotic treatment, in 21% and 37% of conversations, respectively. These findings suggest that affirmation of psychotic ideation significantly varies across different chatbots and does not appear to be an unavoidable consequence of large language model deployment. Furthermore, they underscore the need for developing explicit safety standards governing chatbot responses to psychotic content.

Lasswell's five-question formula remains a durable frame for analyzing source, message, channel, audience and effect. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) underlying mass communication assumptions: intentional human sources, relatively static messages, channels as carries, audiences as receivers and effects as downstream outcomes. This conceptual paper argues for extension rather than abandonment. Its objectives are to examine the model’s analytical adequacy and develop an extension for generative communication. Using scholarship from AI-mediated communication, human-machine communication, algorithmic media, trust and synthetic content and accountability. research to illustrate how these systems can generate, revise, personalize messages (i.e. These competencies allow for the communication of agents that exist as a dispersed network, but ultimately moral agency lies with human and institutional figures. Critical comparative conceptual analysis relates this literature to Lasswell's five questions and integrates the resulting distinctions into a framework. The analysis identifies distributed communicative agency, synthetic and hybrid voice, intelligent mediation, audience co-participation and recursive effects. It distinguishes machine influence from human and institutional responsibility. The proposed framework makes trust appraisal, verification and accountability explicit, with transparency and provenance applying across all stages. Feedback connects outcomes to subsequent production and distribution. It is therefore required as an initial stage of analysis but in times and environments where the source, message and channel can be at least partially artificial, it becomes insufficient. The framework offers concepts for empirical research and practical guidance for documenting authorship, verifying claims and identifying responsible actors in journalism, education and public communication.

Maintaining legacy bioinformatics software remains a longstanding challenge in research computing. Many tools are developed by PhD students and remain in active use long after their graduation, even when the underlying technology stack has become outdated or unsupportable. Yet full rewrites demand substantial developer time, which research group leaders are seldom able to allocate and new recruits are rarely motivated to undertake. Large language model (LLM)-based coding assistants offer a potential new approach to this problem, but their effectiveness in real-world research software engineering (RSE) contexts remains poorly characterized.We present a case study in AI-assisted legacy modernisation using KEGGanim, a Perl CGI web application that overlays time-series gene expression data onto KEGG pathway diagrams as animated visualisations. The tool, originally developed by the BIIT group, was first published in 2008 and has remained available since then. It is currently maintained by the ELIXIR Estonia Node at the University of Tartu as one of ELIXIR Estonia’s Node Services. The tool was rewritten from scratch using Claude Code (Anthropic) as the primary development tool. The new implementation uses FastAPI, React 18, PostgreSQL, and Docker Compose, replacing static GIF output with interactive SVG animations while preserving full data pipeline logic including KEGG gene mapping, ENSG identifier conversion, and KNN imputation.The rewrite was conducted as an instrumented RSE experiment. Development sessions were logged manually for time attribution; all LLM conversation logs were preserved in JSONL format for post-hoc extraction of human intervention counts, token usage, and effort distribution across project phases. Functional correctness was validated using a four-level regression suite against reference fixtures captured from the legacy production instance.We report on the feasibility, efficiency, and failure modes of LLM-driven legacy modernisation, and discuss implications for sustainable tool development within ELIXIR and the wider RSE community.

Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) for picture handling addresses a huge headway in the field of man-made consciousness, democratizing the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods to complex picture related undertakings. Customarily, creating powerful Machine Learning (ML) models for picture handling required broad mastery in information science, model design, and hyper-parameter tuning. AutoML overcomes this issue via mechanizing these unpredictable cycles, making ML open to a more extensive crowd, including those without profound specialized information. At the center of AutoML for picture handling is the mechanization of the whole work process, from information preprocessing to model deployment. The cycle starts with information preprocessing, a basic step that includes setting up the picture information for investigation. This incorporates methods like picture augmentation, where pictures are changed through augmentation, flips, scaling, and variety acclimations to upgrade the variety and power of the dataset. Moreover, standardization guarantees that pixel values are normalized, while resizing and editing change picture aspects to match the model’s feedback prerequisites. When the information is preprocessed, AutoML devices assume control over the difficult errand of model determination. In picture handling, this frequently includes picking either pre-prepared models and custom structures. Pre-prepared models like Visual Geometry Group (VGG) VGG16, ResNet, and Initiation, which have been prepared on huge datasets like ImageNet, are regularly utilized for learning, permitting the new model to use existing information. On the other hand, AutoML can plan custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNNs) custom fitted to the particular picture handling task, advancing the design through mechanized look. The last move toward the AutoML pipeline is model arrangement. AutoML apparatuses work with this by trading the prepared model in designs appropriate for different sending conditions, for example, TensorFlow SavedModel or Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX). Furthermore, procedures like quantization and pruning are applied to upgrade the model for derivation, especially nervous gadgets where computational assets are restricted.

Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has grown significantly since its introduction and inception in the late 1950s and has become interwoven into healthcare. Objective: This narrative review evaluates practice concerns and perceptions associated with the heightened demand for AI in healthcare, particularly as a cost-saving tool for nursing and providers. Methods: Online databases included PubMed and CINAHL. Boolean terminology included healthcare and AI, AI and nursing, as well as AI and ethics. Results were limited to complete online articles written within the previous five years. Initial searches yielded over 55,469 results. Results: Despite a growing push from federal agencies and hospital systems to incorporate their use, there is no definitive consensus on the application of AI in healthcare. This may cause harm to patients as AI tools are not consistently accurate, may misdiagnose, and have potential for "unconscious" bias. However, significant time and cost may be saved with care algorithm implementation. Conclusions: Careful evaluation and ethical analysis are warranted on a case-by-case basis prior to commencement. Nursing staff and healthcare providers are integral to the "care algorithm" and cannot be removed from direct patient care without potential harm.

documents.abstract: Background: Wood-based manufacturing still relies on repetitive manual material handling around CNC workstations, exposing workers to awkward postures, high physical demands, and prolonged standing. At the observed workstation, the primary ergonomic problems were associated with loading, unloading, inspection, and palletizing activities rather than with the machining cycle itself. Objective: This study aimed to address ergonomic issues associated with CNC workstation activities by proposing an ergonomic intervention involving the redesign of a CNC support workstation with a hydraulic lift table. The contribution of this study lies in integrating task-level ergonomic risk assessment with anthropometric design to develop a practical engineering proposal for wood manufacturing. Methods: A quantitative descriptive approach was employed, incorporating direct observation, postural documentation, interviews, Nordic Body Map screening, anthropometric measurements, and the Workplace Ergonomic Risk Assessment (WERA) method. The study involved 14 workers, comprising 5 CNC operators and 9 helpers. Results: The WERA scores were 28 for operators and 41 for helpers, indicating greater ergonomic risk exposure among helpers. The predominant risk factors were shoulder posture, neck posture, forceful exertion, repetition, and task duration. Anthropometric analysis informed the proposed design of a hydraulic lift table with a platform measuring 1,300 × 1,100 mm, an adjustable height range of 300–900 mm, and a minimum lifting capacity of 100 kg. Conclusion: Helper tasks represent the most critical source of ergonomic risk at the CNC workstation. The proposed hydraulic lift table offers a feasible engineering intervention to reduce ergonomic risks and support occupational health and safety in wood manufacturing.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Personalised robot tutoring requires real-time pedagogical decision-making under uncertain and multimodal learner states. Existing intelligent tutoring and robot-assisted learning systems often rely on static rules, single-modality learner modelling, or short-term correctness-oriented optimisation, which limits their capacity to balance knowledge acquisition, engagement, retention, and safe embodied interaction. RL-Robotutor is presented as a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that integrates cognitive knowledge-tracing signals, facial-expression and gaze-derived affective cues, and behavioural interaction logs through transformer-based fusion. A PPO-trained meta-policy selects among specialised modules for learner assessment, curriculum adaptation, strategy selection, and reflective feedback, while a hybrid reward combines immediate learning performance, engagement, long-term learning gain, and safety. The evidence is reported by source: five public knowledge-tracing datasets assess the cognitive prediction component; controlled simulator experiments assess policy learning, reward ablation, and multimodal fusion; and a randomised robot-tutoring study assesses embodied interaction with 120 undergraduate participants. RL-Robotutor outperforms rule-based, flat reinforcement-learning, knowledge-tracing, and LLM-based comparators. In the human study, the learning gain is 0.62, compared with 0.40 for the rule-based robot condition. The full hybrid reward improves simulator learning gain by 19% over correctness-only optimisation, and full multimodal fusion improves simulator engagement by 17% over text-only modelling. Jetson Orin deployment achieves 48 ms inference latency with an absolute AUC reduction of 0.007, supporting real-time edge execution.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Background and Aims: Students with dyslexia face challenges in reading and writing, particularly when learning Traditional Chinese. This study designs and implements LexiBo, a supplementary robot-assisted language learning (RALL) system tailored to Cantonese instruction students, informed by self-determination theory (SDT) and expectancy-value theory (EVT), and assesses using SDT, EVT, and intrinsic motivation inventory (IMI) questionnaires to foster learning motivation.Sample: This is a 30-week experiment with sixty-eight participants, including control (dyslexia: N = 18, without dyslexia: N = 18) and experimental groups (dyslexia: N = 16, without dyslexia: N = 16).Methods: A mixed-methods analysis of questionnaires, proficiency tests, and interviews is employed.Results: Students with dyslexia demonstrate statistically significant improvement in emotional engagement, intrinsic motivation, and learning performance over time. RALL also appears to reduce affective barriers in intervention while supporting students' ability and expectancy beliefs.Originality: This study integrates SDT and EVT into RALL for Cantonese-speaking students. The system addresses the under-researched cognitive and affective barriers of acquiring a tonal and logographic language through a comprehensive longitudinal design.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed content marketing by enabling the creation of personalized, scalable, and data-driven marketing content.This study aims to examine the role of generative AI in content marketing and its impact on consumer perception and brand interaction.The research adopts a descriptive and analytical design, using primary data collected from 120 respondents who actively engage with digital platforms.A structured questionnaire based on a five-point Likert scale was employed to measure key constructs, including generative AI content quality, consumer perception, perceived authenticity, trust, and brand interaction.The collected data were analysed using SPSS, applying statistical techniques such as reliability analysis, factor analysis, correlation, and regression.The findings reveal that generative AI-driven content has a significant positive impact on consumer perception and brand interaction.The study also highlights that perceived authenticity plays a crucial role in building consumer trust, which in turn strongly influences brand interaction.Furthermore, consumer perception and trust partially mediate the relationship between AI-generated content and brand interaction.While generative AI enhances marketing efficiency and engagement, concerns related to authenticity and trust remain important considerations.The study contributes to the existing literature by providing empirical evidence on the effectiveness of generative AI in content marketing and offers practical insights for marketers to develop balanced strategies that integrate technological capabilities with human creativity.The findings are particularly relevant for organizations seeking to enhance consumer engagement and build sustainable brand relationships in the evolving digital marketing landscape.

As frontier large language models transition from monolithic dense networks to sparsely gated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, determining architectural provenance in black-box text has become a critical forensic challenge. Existing detectors operate under binary paradigms (human vs. machine) or require token-level probability logits that are suppressed by commercial API gateways. In this short paper, we present an empirical investigation into whether sparse expert routing leaves an indelible post-hoc syntactic signature in generated prose. Evaluating across N=120 verified long-form corporate documents (>=750 words, mean 1,050.0 words) spanning three frontier MoE architectures (DeepSeek-V3 671B, Nemotron-3 Super 120B, MiniMax-01 456B) and three frontier Dense architectures (Qwen-2.5 72B, Llama-3.3 70B, Cohere Command-R+ 104B), we evaluate discrimination across clausal subordination entropy (H_clause) and macro-discursive coherence decay (Delta_decay). Our empirical results demonstrate: (1) Binary MoE vs. Dense architectural segregation achieves an AUROC of 0.9897 (94.13% accuracy) on unperturbed text, remaining stable at 0.9424 AUROC (84.40% accuracy) under aggressive 11B DIPPER neural paraphrasing (L=60, O=60). (2) Within isolated cohorts, fine-grained model attribution achieves 90.00% Top-1 accuracy across MoE architectures (DeepSeek vs. Nemotron vs. MiniMax; Top-2 Recall: 100.0%) and 80.00% Top-1 accuracy across Dense architectures (Qwen vs. Llama vs. Cohere; Top-2 Recall: 100.0%). (3) In global 6-way attribution (n=60), the framework achieves 73.33% Top-1 accuracy (Mean Reciprocal Rank 0.8306 vs. 0.1667 random chance; permutation p = 0.0010), maintaining 68.33% Top-1 accuracy under strict Leave-One-Topic-Out out-of-domain cross-validation. These findings confirm that sparse mixture routing imprints distinct clausal branching dynamics that survive vocabulary substitution.

The study investigated the appraisal of safety incidents among workers in selected oil and gas downstream companies in Port Harcourt metropolis. The study design was a descriptive survey design and study population consisted of 1500 workers oil and gas downstream companies in Port Harcourt. A non-stratified sampling method was used in selecting the sample of the study which consisted of 340 workers. A self- structured questionnaire was the instrument of the study. The study found that 56% of the respondents were 25-30 years old, 28% were 31 – 35 years old, 14% were 36 – 40 years old while 2% were 41 years old above, 78% of the respondents were males while 22% were females. The study further revealed that the types of safety incidents that were common among workers in oil and gas downstream companies in Port Harcourt metropolis includes truck tanker accident in transit, Truck tanker accident within the terminal or station etc and that the injuries that are common in oil and gas downstream companies in Port Harcourt metropolis includes back injury (ergonomic), sprain of a limb etc. The study concluded that workers at different levels in the Port Harcourt metropolis oil and gas downstream sector experienced safety incidents. Therefore, the study recommended that companies particularly, petroleum products retailers should commit to developing sound HSE culture among workers by way of robust HSE policies and personnel training programs. These programs would address both unsafe practices and unsafe situations.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Recent fatal accidents in aviation have once again highlighted the critical importance of safety and the need for continuous advancement in safety management approaches. Over the years, the accumulation of vast amounts of safety data and information has not only enhanced our understanding of operational risks but has also introduced new challenges related to data complexity, interpretation, and effective utilization. The increasing complexity of aviation operations, coupled with the rapid growth of data-driven technologies, has further challenged traditional safety management approaches that are predominantly reactive and compliance-based.In this context, the concept of safety intelligence has emerged as a promising paradigm that transforms raw operational data into actionable insights for proactive and predictive safety decision-making. This review article synthesizes existing literature on safety intelligence, safety management systems, human factors, and data analytics to provide a comprehensive conceptual understanding of safety intelligence in aviation. Particular attention is given to the integration of data-driven approaches with human interpretation, organizational learning, and safety culture.The ultimate goal of this line of research has become increasingly evident in light of recent aviation accidents, emphasizing the need for a deeper and more holistic understanding of safety intelligence to enhance global flight safety.

Space debris poses a significant threat to space missions, requiring accurate and real-time detection across multiple orbital regimes and observation platforms. This study aims to develop a scalable YOLOv12-PSO framework for accurate space debris detection and to investigate its effectiveness in improving real-time performance, robustness, and detection accuracy across orbital environments. A publicly available space debris image dataset containing synthetic and real images was used to train and evaluate the proposed framework under varying orbital conditions. The proposed system integrates YOLOv12 with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for hyperparameter tuning, while preprocessing steps such as resizing, normalization, and data augmentation are applied to improve robustness. The model is trained and tested on the dataset for object detection, optimization, and performance assessment. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized model outperforms baseline approaches, achieving Precision (0.89), Recall (0.87), F1-Score (0.88), and mAP (0.78). Comparative evaluation against Baseline YOLOV12, YOLOV12v8m, YOLOV12v8s, YOLOV12v5s, GEO-SPANN, and CNN-based methods confirms improved detection accuracy and real-time inference performance under noisy and complex conditions. This work presents a novel scalable deep learning framework integrating YOLOv12 with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), enhancing detection accuracy, efficiency, and robustness, while contributing to advanced space situational awareness systems, autonomous space debris monitoring, and improved orbital debris mitigation and management strategies. The proposed YOLOv12-PSO framework supports autonomous space debris monitoring and provides a policy-relevant tool for space traffic management, contributing to improved orbital safety, collision risk reduction, and long-term sustainability of space mission operations and satellite environment governance.

Generative AI is reshaping how research software is developed. Tools and patterns ranging from “vibe coding” through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and autonomous agents now offer compelling productivity gains, but their adoption in scientific computing surfaces failure modes that general-purpose evaluation does not catch: silent unit conversions, violated conservation laws, hallucinated physics, loss of numerical precision, and quietly broken reproducibility. These failures share a signature: nothing visible goes wrong. The AI ecosystem itself is moving fast, leaving RSEs to make consequential integration decisions with little shared vocabulary or principled guidance. This talk introduces Scientific Agentic Engineering, the central contribution of an in-progress 2026 Better Scientific Software (BSSw) Fellowship: a tool-agnostic methodology for integrating AI agents into high-stakes scientific software workflows. The framework defines how agents, scientific skills, and MCP servers should be structured around validation loops, explicit human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and domain-specific safeguards. Every task moves through a short workflow (frame, plan and critique, implement, verify), with decisions recorded throughout, and the framework maps each documented failure mode to the stage where it is cheapest to catch. The intent is not to recommend any particular AI tool but to articulate foundational concepts that remain valid as the underlying technology changes. I will share three artifacts from the fellowship: The Framework (published July 2026). Shared vocabulary, its principles and workflow, structural guidance on where safeguards live, and a pattern catalog of named practices, each tied to the failure it counters. The Reference Workflow. A structured exercise in which RSEs use AI tools to build a small weather-model error-statistics application, applying the framework to avoid the failure modes it documents. The Community Repository.
